Avodah Zarah 4a:11.english: With regard to the afflictions of the Jewish people, the Gemara relates: Rabbi Abbahu would praise Rav Safra to the heretics by saying that he is a great man. Therefore, they remitted Rav Safra’s obligation to pay taxes for thirteen years, as they relied upon Rabbi Abbahu’s word and wanted to reward a great man. One day they found Rav Safra and said to him: It is written: “You only have I known of all the families of the earth; therefore, I will visit upon you all your iniquities” (Amos 3:2). One who has wrath [siseya], does He, God, raise it against His beloved? Rav Safra was silent and did not say anything in response to them. The heretics threw a scarf around Rav Safra’s neck and tormented him, by pulling and denigrating him.

Avodah Zarah 4a:14.english: The heretics said to Rabbi Abbahu: In that case, you should tell us the meaning of this verse. Rabbi Abbahu said to them: I will relate a parable to you. To what is this matter comparable? It is comparable to a person who lends money to two people, one of whom is his beloved, and the other one is his enemy. In the case of his beloved, the lender collects the debt from the beloved little by little, whereas in the case of his enemy, he, the lender, collects the debt from the enemy all at once. So too, with regard to the Jewish people, God punishes the Jews for each transgression as it occurs, so that they should not receive one severe punishment on a single occasion.

Avodah Zarah 4a:17.english: The Gemara raises a difficulty: But is it true that one who is completely righteous cannot be destroyed along with the wicked? But isn’t it written in a prophecy about the destruction of the Temple that God says to the destroyers: “And begin at My Sanctuary [mimmikdashi]” (Ezekiel 9:6); and Rav Yosef teaches: Do not read the word as “mimmikdashi,” but rather read it as mimmekudashai, those sanctified to Me. He explains: These are people who observed the Torah in its entirety, from the first letter of the Hebrew alphabet alef through its final letter tav. These people observed every mitzva in the Torah, and yet the righteous were destroyed along with the wicked. The Gemara answers the difficulty: There too, since the righteous had the power to protest against the wicked and prevent the wicked from sinning and the righteous did not protest, they are considered as righteous people who are not completely righteous.

Avodah Zarah 4a:4.english: Rav Ḥinnana bar Pappa raises a contradiction between the following verses. It is written: “The Almighty, Whom we have not found out His excellent power” (Job 37:23), which indicates that God's power has not been seen. And it is written elsewhere: “Great is our Lord, and mighty in power” (Psalms 147:5), and it is also written: “Your right hand, O Lord, glorious in power” (Exodus 15:6), from which it may be inferred that God's power is discernable. The Gemara answers: This is not difficult; here, in the first verse, God’s strength is not seen at a time of judgment, where God acts mercifully, whereas there, in the other verses, the verses refer to a time of war, when God wages war against His enemies and His power is seen.

Avodah Zarah 4b:1.english: “And knows the knowledge of the Most High” (Numbers 24:16). Now, this should not be understood to mean that Balaam knew the thoughts of God, as is it possible that Balaam did not know the mind of his animal, and yet he, Balaam, did know the mind of the Most High?

Avodah Zarah 4b:10.english: In explanation of the cause of God’s anger, it is taught in the name of Rabbi Meir: When the kings wake up and place their crowns on their heads and bow down to the sun, the Holy One, Blessed be He, immediately grows angry. This is why God’s anger occurs during the first three hours of the day. Rav Yosef says: A person should not recite the additional prayers during the first three hours of the day on the first day of Rosh HaShana if he is praying individually, as, since the judgment of the entire world is reckoned then, perhaps the Heavenly court will scrutinize that person's actions and reject him.

Avodah Zarah 4b:14.english: The Gemara presents a mnemonic for the ensuing statements of Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi: Day, bear witness, strike, in the calf. The Gemara returns to the matter itself mentioned earlier (3a). Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi says: What is the meaning of that which is written: “Which I command you this day, to do them” (Deuteronomy 7:11)? “Today to do them,” but not tomorrow, in the World-to-Come, to do them. “Today to do them,” but not today to receive their reward, as reward is granted in the World-to-Come.

Avodah Zarah 4b:15.english: Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi says: All of the mitzvot that the Jews perform in this world will come and bear witness for them in the World-to-Come, as it is stated: “Let them bring their witnesses that they may be justified, and let them hear, and say: It is truth” (Isaiah 43:9). He explains: “Let them bring their witnesses that they may be justified”; these are referring to the Jews. “And let them hear, and say: It is truth”; these are referring to the nations of the world.

Avodah Zarah 4b:16.english: And Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi says: All of the mitzvot that the Jewish people perform in this world will come and strike the nations of the world on their faces in the World-to-Come, as it is stated: “Observe therefore and do them; for this is your wisdom and your understanding in the eyes of the nations” (Deuteronomy 4:6). It is not stated: Before the nations; rather, the verse states: “In the eyes of the nations,” which taken literally teaches that the mitzvot will come and strike the nations of the world on their faces in the World-to-Come.

Avodah Zarah 4b:17.english: And Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi says: The Jewish people fashioned the Golden Calf only to give an opening for the claim of penitents, as it is stated after the revelation at Sinai: “Who would give that they had such a heart as this always, to fear Me, and keep all My commandments, that it might be good for them, and with their children forever” (Deuteronomy 5:26). If the nation was truly at such a lofty spiritual state, how could they worship the Golden Calf? Rather, their sin occurred so that it would be made clear that one can repent for any sin, as even a sin as severe as the Golden Calf was forgiven.

Avodah Zarah 4b:18.english: And this is similar to that which Rabbi Yoḥanan says in the name of Rabbi Shimon ben Yoḥai: David was not fit for that deed, and the Jewish people were not fit for that deed of the Golden Calf. David was not fit for that deed involving Bathsheba, as it is written: “And my heart is wounded [ḥalal] within me” (Psalms 109:22), i.e., King David had slain his evil inclination, and therefore it should not have been able to rule over him to that extent.

Avodah Zarah 4b:19.english: And likewise the Jewish people were not fit for that deed of the Golden Calf, as it is written with regard to the Jewish people of that time: “Who would give that they had such a heart as this always, to fear Me and keep all My commandments, that it might be good for them, and with their children forever” (Deuteronomy 5:26). Rather, why did the Jewish people do these sins?

Avodah Zarah 4b:8.english: The Gemara relates: A certain heretic would distress Rabi Yehoshua ben Levi by incessantly challenging him as to the meaning of verses. One day, Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi took a rooster and placed it between the legs of the bed upon which he sat, and looked at it. Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi thought: When that moment of God’s anger arrives, I will curse the heretic and be rid of him. When that moment of God’s anger arrived, Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi fell asleep and missed the opportunity to curse the heretic.

Rashi on Avodah Zarah 4a:11:1.english: "I have known" - [Meaning] I have loved, as in (Psalms 1:6): "The Lord knows the way of the righteous," and as in (Exodus 33:17): "And I have known you by name."

Rashi on Avodah Zarah 4a:11:3.hebrew: ברחמיה מסיק ליה - מעלהו על אוהבו. "והנם זועפים" (בראשית מ, ו) מתרגמינן נסיסין. לשון אחר: סוסיא - סוס שעסקו רע, את אוהבו מעלין עליו כדי שימות:
Rashi on Avodah Zarah 4a:11:3.english: Raise it against his beloved - [Does He] bring it up against His beloved? [And with regard to the verse (Genesis 40:6):] "And behold, they were sad," the Targum translates it as nesisin. Another explanation: Suseya [means] a horse whose behavior is bad; [does one] make his beloved ride upon it so that he might die?

Rashi on Avodah Zarah 4a:14:1.hebrew: נפרע ממנו מעט מעט - כן ישראל: נפרע מהן הקדוש ברוך הוא את כל עונותיהן בעולם הזה כדי שיזכו ליום הדין; ועובדי כוכבים אינו נפרע מהן כלל כדי לטרדן מן העולם הבא. ופקידה משמע מעט מעט, כאדם שפוקד את חבירו לפרקים:
Rashi on Avodah Zarah 4a:14:1.english: Collects from him little by little - So it is with Israel: The Holy One, Blessed be He, takes retribution from them for all their iniquities in this world so that they should merit [acquittal on] the Day of Judgment; but from idolaters He does not take retribution at all [now], in order to banish them from the World-to-Come. And pekida [visitation] implies [doing so] little by little, like a person who visits his friend occasionally.

Rashi on Avodah Zarah 4a:17:1.english: "And begin at My Sanctuary" - This is written in Ezekiel regarding the four destroyers who came to destroy Jerusalem.

Rashi on Avodah Zarah 4a:18:1.english: "Indignation every day" - And even so [the people] remain [alive], yet it is written: "Who can stand?"

Rashi on Avodah Zarah 4a:18:2.english: For an individual - [The verse asks:] "Who can stand?"

Rashi on Avodah Zarah 4a:18:3.english: For the community - Even though He has indignation every day, they remain [alive].

Rashi on Avodah Zarah 4a:4:1.english: "We have not found Him to be of excellent power" at the time of judgment - If He were to manifest His power, everyone would be liable to destruction.

Rashi on Avodah Zarah 4a:5:1.hebrew: רבי אחא בר חנינא אמר: תרוייהו בישראל - והכי קאמר: אע"פ שבעל חימה אני, חימה אין לי; כבר נשבעתי מקצוף עליך:
Rashi on Avodah Zarah 4a:5:1.english: Rabbi Acha bar Chanina said: Both [verses refer] to Israel - And this is what the verse means: Even though I am a possessor of fury, I have no fury [now], for I have already sworn not to be wroth with you.

Rashi on Avodah Zarah 4a:5:2.english: "Would that I" - This is the conclusion of this verse.

Rashi on Avodah Zarah 4a:5:3.hebrew: שמיר ושית - לשון ארץ גזירה וחורבן; ודוגמתו (איכה ג) השאת והשבר:
Rashi on Avodah Zarah 4a:5:3.english: "Briers and thorns" - An expression for a land of being cut off and destruction, and its equivalent is (Lamentations 3:47): "The devastation and the destruction."

Rashi on Avodah Zarah 4a:6:1.english: "And this is what Rabbi Alexandri [says]" - This refers to what was said above, that the Holy One, Blessed be He, does not deal tyrannically with His creatures.

Rashi on Avodah Zarah 4a:6:2.english: In their records [benigeni] - In the book of remembrance of their deeds.

Rashi on Avodah Zarah 4a:6:3.english: "And if not, I will destroy them" - And I will visit punishment upon them with strict judgment and not with compassion, but rather with precision, as we said above: He heats the sun over them from its sheath, perhaps they will kick [the sukka].

Rashi on Avodah Zarah 4a:7:1.english: "And this is also what Rava says" - That the Holy One, Blessed be He, judges idolaters with precision.

Rashi on Avodah Zarah 4a:7:2.english: "A ruin, a ruin, a ruin, will I make it" - Perverting [they] perverted, and for [their] perversion I will make it [a ruin]; and similarly Targum Yonatan [translates it]: "Their sins they sinned; through their sins I will take retribution from them."

Rashi on Avodah Zarah 4a:7:3.hebrew: כפיד - ניקור, ביקדור"א בלע"ז, שמנקרין מעט מעט. וכן נפרע מהן מעט מעט בהסתר פנים, ב"והיה לאכול", לפדותם מעונותיהן כדי שיזכו לעולם הבא:
Rashi on Avodah Zarah 4a:7:3.english: Like the pecking [kefid] - A pecking, becquedure in Old French, as they peck little by little. And similarly, He takes retribution from Israel little by little through the hiding of His face, in the sense of "and it shall be for devouring," to redeem them from their iniquities so that they may merit the World-to-Come.

Rashi on Avodah Zarah 4a:8:1.english: "They will be saved [lahen shua]" - I give to them a redemption, like (Exodus 14:30): "And He saved [vayosha]" and redeemed, and like (Bava Kamma 80a): "Yeshua habben," meaning redemption.

Rashi on Avodah Zarah 4a:9:1.hebrew: והיינו דאמר רבי אבא - אפדם לישראל בממונם; והיינו כפיד של תרנגולין: פורעין מעט מעט. ונוגשיך בצדקה:
Rashi on Avodah Zarah 4a:9:1.english: And this is what Rabbi Abba says - I will redeem Israel through their money; and this is like the pecking of hens: They pay little by little. [And this relates to the verse:] "And your taskmasters [in] righteousness" (Isaiah 60:17).

Rashi on Avodah Zarah 4b:10:1.english: During the first three hours - During the hour of [divine] wrath.

Rashi on Avodah Zarah 4b:13:1.english: "Buy the truth" - Spend money on the study of Torah.

Rashi on Avodah Zarah 4b:13:2.english: "And sell it not" - Teach others for free.

Rashi on Avodah Zarah 4b:13:3.hebrew: דין לא כתיב ביה אמת - והא דכתיב (תהילים יט, י): "משפטי ה' אמת", במשפטים הכתובים בתורה וציום לישראל קא משתעי, דלעיל מיניה כתיב "פקודי ה' ישרים". מוספי כל השנה הן שבח וסיפורי מעשה; אבל מוסף ראש השנה, מתוך שהוא מתפלל מלכיות, זכרונות, שופרות - מיפקד דינא טפי, ואל יפרוש אדם עצמו מן הצבור:
Rashi on Avodah Zarah 4b:13:3.english: Judgment, with regard to which it is not written: Truth - And that which is written (Psalms 19:10): "The judgments of the Lord are truth," [that] is speaking about the judgments written in the Torah that He commanded to Israel, for above it it is written: "The precepts of the Lord are right." [Rashi adds:] The additional prayers of the entire year are [composed of] praise and the telling of deeds; but the additional prayer of Rosh HaShana, because one prays Kingships, Remembrances, and Shofarot, the judgment is reckoned more, and a person should not separate himself from the community.

Rashi on Avodah Zarah 4b:14:1.hebrew: ולא למחר לעשותם - שאין מצוות לעתיד:", "english": "“And not tomorrow to do them” – for there are no mitzvot in the future (the World-to-Come).

Rashi on Avodah Zarah 4b:17:1.hebrew: לא עשו ישראל את העגל - כלומר: גיבורים ושליטים ביצרם היו, ולא היה ראוי להתגבר יצרם עליהן; אלא גזירת מלך היתה לשלוט בם, כדי ליתן פתחון פה לבעלי תשובה, שאם יאמר החוטא: "לא אשוב, שלא יקבלני", אומרים לו: "צא ולמד ממעשה העגל, שכפרו ונתקבלו בתשובה":", "english": "“The Jewish people did not fashion the Calf” – meaning, they were heroes and masters over their inclination, and it was not fitting for their inclination to overcome them. Rather, it was a decree of the King for it to rule over them, in order to give an opening for penitents, so that if a sinner says: “I will not repent because God will not accept me,” they say to him: “Go and learn from the incident of the Calf, for the Jewish people acted heretically and yet were accepted in repentance.”

Rashi on Avodah Zarah 4b:17:2.hebrew: מי יתן והיה לבבם זה וגו' - בסיני נאמר; אלמא גיבורים ואמיצי לבב ביראתם היו:", "english": "“Who would give that they had such a heart as this, etc.” – This was said at Sinai; consequently, the Jewish people were heroes and strong-hearted in their fear of God."

Rashi on Avodah Zarah 4b:18:1.hebrew: לאותו מעשה - של בת שבע:", "english": "“[For] that incident” – of Bathsheba."

Rashi on Avodah Zarah 4b:18:2.hebrew: לבי חלל - יצר הרע חלל בקרבי, ואין לו כוח לשלוט בקרבי:", "english": "“My heart is wounded [ḥalal]” – the evil inclination was as though slain [ḥalal] within me, and it had no power to rule within me."

Rashi on Avodah Zarah 4b:1:1.english: "And knows the mind of the Most High" - This implies [he knew it] on his own and not through prophecy, and therefore [the Gemara] asks: [Is it possible he] did not know the mind of his animal?

Rashi on Avodah Zarah 4b:2:2.english: I left it [shadai lei] - I sent it [the horse] to graze.

Rashi on Avodah Zarah 4b:4:1.english: "From Shittim unto Gilgal" - Until your arrival at Gilgal, where I struck down your enemies before you.

Rashi on Avodah Zarah 4b:6:1.english: "For His anger is but for a moment" - Hence [it is derived] that a moment is [the duration of] His anger.

Rashi on Avodah Zarah 4b:7:1.english: During the first three hours - During the hour of [divine] wrath.

Rashi on Avodah Zarah 4b:9:1.english: Not proper conduct - To determine the hour of His wrath.

Tosafot on Avodah Zarah 4a:17:1.hebrew: שהיה בידם למחות - והא דאמרינן בסוף חזקת הבתים (בבא בתרא דף ס:) "מוטב שיהיו שוגגין ואל יהיו מזידין", היינו בדבר שידוע שלא יקבלו אם ימחו:
Tosafot on Avodah Zarah 4a:17:1.english: Since they had the power to protest - And that which we say at the end of [the chapter] Hezkat Habbatim (Bava Batra 60b): "It is better that they be unwitting [sinners] and not be intentional [sinners]," that applies to a matter where it is known that they will not accept [the rebuke] if one protests.

Tosafot on Avodah Zarah 4a:5:1.hebrew: חימה אין לי שכבר נשבעתי - ואין להקשות מפרק ד' (דף לב.) נדרים, דמוכח דמשה הרגו לחימה, דאיכא לשנויי: תרי חימה הוו; כדמשני נמי התם:
Tosafot on Avodah Zarah 4a:5:1.english: "Fury is not in Me," as I have already taken an oath - And one should not raise a difficulty from the fourth chapter of Nedarim (32a), which proves that Moses killed [the angel of] Fury, for it is possible to answer that there were two [angels named] Fury, as is also answered there.

Tosafot on Avodah Zarah 4a:6:1.hebrew: והיינו דרבי אלכסנדרי - פירוש הקונטרס דקאי אההיא דקאמרינן לעיל דאין הקדוש ברוך הוא בא בטרוניא עם בריותיו, ולא נהירא פירושו דהא איפסיק ליה טובא. ונראה לרבינו תם דקאי אהא דסליק: "כאן בישראל כאן בעובדי כוכבים", וקאמרינן ד"בעל חימה" קאי אעובדי כוכבים. והיינו דרבי אלכסנדרי דקאמר: "ביום ההוא אבקש", שאם לא ימצא להם זכות ישמידם. והיינו נמי דרבא דאמר שיש חילוק בין ישראל לעובדי כוכבים:
Tosafot on Avodah Zarah 4a:6:1.english: And this is what Rabbi Alexandri [says] - Rashi explains that this refers to that which we said above, that the Holy One, Blessed be He, does not deal tyrannically with His creatures. But his explanation is not satisfactory, for it is separated [from that statement] by too much [text]. Rather, it appears to Rabbeinu Tam that it refers to that which concluded: "Here with regard to Israel, there with regard to the nations," and we say that "the possessor of fury" refers to the nations. And this is what Rabbi Alexandri [says] when he said: "In that day I will seek," that if He does not find merit for them, He will destroy them. And this is also what Rava [says], that there is a difference between Israel and the nations.

Tosafot on Avodah Zarah 4a:6:2.hebrew: בניגני שלהם - פירוש: במעשה שלהם. "מה נורא מעשיך" (תהילים סו, ג) מתרגמינן: מה דחילין אינון מניגניא דילך:
Tosafot on Avodah Zarah 4a:6:2.english: In their records [benigeni] - Meaning, in their deeds. [As the verse states:] “How awesome are Your works [ma’asekha]” (Psalms 66:3), [which] we translate [in the Targum] as: “How awesome are Your nigenaya.”

Tosafot on Avodah Zarah 4b:11:1.hebrew: כיון דאיכא צבורא דמצלי לא מדחי - פירוש רבינו תם: הא דמשמע הכא דמהני אפילו כשהצבור מתפללין במקום אחר, היינו דוקא דלא מדחי, אבל אינה נשמעת אלא במקום שהצבור מתפללין, כדאמרינן בפרק קמא דברכות (דף ו.): "אין תפלתו של אדם נשמעת אלא עם הצבור":
Tosafot on Avodah Zarah 4b:11:1.english: Since there is a community that prays, his prayer is not rejected - Rabbeinu Tam explains that that which is implied here, that it is effective even when the community is praying in a different place, that applies specifically [to the fact] that it is not rejected; but it is not heard [favorably] except in the place where the community prays, as we say in the first chapter of Berakhot (6a): "A person’s prayer is only heard [favorably] with the community."

Tosafot on Avodah Zarah 4b:1:1.english: "And knows the mind of the Most High" - This implies [he knew it] on his own and not through prophecy, and therefore [the Gemara] asks: [Is it possible he] did not know the mind of his animal?

Tosafot on Avodah Zarah 4b:6:1.hebrew: רגע כמימרא - ואם תאמר: מה היה יכול לומר בשעה מועטת כזאת? ויש לומר: היה אומר "כלם", והקדוש ברוך הוא הפכו ואמר "מלך", כדכתיב (במדבר כג, כא) "ותרועת מלך בו". ורבי אליהו היה מפרש שאין צריך רק להתחיל קללתו באותו רגע; תדע שהיה רוצה להאריך בקללתו, כדאיתא ב"חלק" (סנהדרין דף קה:): "מברכותיו של אותו רשע אתה למד מה היה בלבו":
Tosafot on Avodah Zarah 4b:6:1.english: "A moment [rega] as [long as it takes] to say [it]" - And if you ask: What could he have said in such a small amount of time? One can answer: He was going to say "Destroy them [kallem]," and the Holy One, Blessed be He, overturned it and said "King [melekh]," as it is written (Numbers 23:21): "And the shout of a king [melekh] is among them." And Rabbi Eliyahu was explaining that he only needed to begin his curse in that moment. You should know that he wanted to lengthen his curse, as is found in [chapter] Helek (Sanhedrin 105b): "From the blessings of that wicked man you can learn what was in his heart."

Tosafot on Avodah Zarah 4b:6:2.english: Thus we should read: "And from where do we derive that God’s anger lasts for a moment? As it is written: 'His anger is but for a moment'" - And we should not read: "And from where do we derive that a moment is as long as it takes to say it," for if so, how could he derive from this verse that a moment is as long as it takes to say it?

Tosafot on Avodah Zarah 4b:7:1.hebrew: בתלת שעי קמייתא - פירוש: בשלישית, כדאמרינן בסמוך: בשעה שהחמה זורחת מלכי מזרח ומערב מניחים את כתריהן. ודרכן של מלכים לעמוד בשלוש שעות, כדאמרינן בפרק קמא דברכות (דף ט:):
Tosafot on Avodah Zarah 4b:7:1.english: During the first three hours - Meaning in the third [hour], as we say later: At the hour that the sun shines, the kings of the East and West place their crowns [on their heads]. And it is the way of kings to rise in the third hour, as we say in the first chapter of Berakhot (9b).

Tosafot on Avodah Zarah 4b:9:1.hebrew: שמע מינה לאו אורח ארעא - לספרים דגרסינן: "ההוא עובד כוכבים", ניחא, דעובדי כוכבים לא מעלין ולא מורידין (לקמן עבודה זרה דף כו.), והוא שבקש לקללו להזיקו בקללתו נתכוין ולא להרגו; ולא דמי להורדה לבור. ואפילו לספרים דגרסי: "ההוא מינא", אע"פ שהכופרים מורידין לבור, נמי ניחא, דודאי ביקש להרוג בקללתו. ומכל מקום קאמר בתר הכי: "שמע מינה לאו אורח ארעא", כי לא היה לו לדחוק בידי שמים ולהעניש מי שאינם רוצים להעניש, אע"פ שבזמן הבית היה מותר להרגו בידים:
Tosafot on Avodah Zarah 4b:9:1.english: Conclude from here that it is not proper conduct - For the books that read "a certain gentile" [instead of "heretic"], it is satisfactory, as "idolaters are neither raised [from a pit] nor lowered [into one]" (26b), and he sought to curse him to harm him with his curse and not to kill him; and it is not comparable to lowering [someone] into a pit. And even for the books that read "a certain heretic," even though heretics are "lowered into a pit" [to their death], it is also satisfactory, for certainly he sought to kill [him] with his curse. And nevertheless, [the Gemara] says afterward: "Conclude from here that it is not proper conduct," for he should not have pressed upon the hands of Heaven to punish someone whom they do not wish to punish, even though during the time of the Temple it was permitted to kill him manually.
